docs.title: Fixing Greyed-Out Cowork Tab on Windows 11
Fixing Greyed-Out Cowork Tab on Windows 11
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Use this reference if Claude Desktop shows a Chat / Cowork slider, but you can't select "Cowork" — it stays greyed out.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Cowork runs inside an isolated Hyper-V-based VM. This requires:

  • Windows 11 Pro, Enterprise, or Education. Windows 11 Home doesn't support Hyper-V (it's missing the vmms service), so Cowork can never be enabled on Home edition.
  • Hyper-V enabled at the OS level.
  • A specific driver (vfpext.sys) actually deployed on disk. This can silently fail even when Hyper-V reports as "Enabled."
  • Hardware virtualization enabled in BIOS/UEFI (Intel VT-x / AMD-V / SVM Mode).
  • A paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise).

docs.title: Step 1: Upgrade Windows Home to Pro
docs.text: If you're on Windows 11 Home, upgrade first through the Microsoft Store ("Upgrade to Windows 10/11 Pro"). This is a license upgrade, not a reinstall — your files and apps stay intact.

docs.title: Step 2: Check Whether Hyper-V's Core Service Exists
docs.text:
Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:

Get-Service vmms

If you see Cannot find any service with service name 'vmms', Hyper-V isn't installed yet.

docs.title: Step 3: Enable Hyper-V
docs.text:
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Hyper-V -All

This takes a few minutes and prompts a restart. Save your work and reboot when it's done.

docs.title: Step 4: Confirm Hyper-V Is Running After Reboot
docs.text:
Get-Service vmms

The status should now show Running.

Fully quit Claude Desktop (tray icon → Quit, not just closing the window) and relaunch it. If Cowork is still greyed out — common if Claude Desktop was installed before Hyper-V existed on the machine — uninstall and reinstall Claude Desktop from claude.com/download, accepting the Windows UAC prompt during install. This registers the Cowork virtualization service machine-wide.

docs.title: Step 5: Resolve a "Missing HCS Services: vfpext" Error
docs.text:
If hovering over the disabled Cowork tab shows "Missing HCS services: vfpext," this is a known Windows/Hyper-V driver deployment bug — the vfpext.sys driver (used for Hyper-V's virtual networking) fails to get copied to disk, even though Hyper-V reports as enabled.

Check the virtualization firmware status:

Get-ComputerInfo -Property "HyperV*"

Confirm HyperVisorPresent : True and that virtualization firmware is enabled in BIOS.

Then confirm the driver file is actually missing:

Test-Path C:\Windows\System32\drivers\vfpext.sys

If this returns False, the driver genuinely wasn't deployed — this matches the bug pattern.

docs.title: Step 6: Fix the Missing Driver
docs.text:
Run these in order, rebooting and re-checking vfpext.sys after each stage:

  1. Enable related virtualization features: 
    Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Containers -All
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName VirtualMachinePlatform -All
    Restart the PC.
  2. If still missing, run a DISM repair (can take 10–20 minutes): 
    DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
    Restart and re-check.
  3. If still missing, run a system file check: 
    sfc /scannow
  4. Also worth trying: clear Claude Desktop's cache through Help → Troubleshoot → Restart. In some cases the underlying components were actually fine, but Claude's own detection was stale.

docs.title: Step 7: Verify the Fix
docs.text:
Test-Path C:\Windows\System32\drivers\vfpext.sys

This should now return True.

Fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop. The Cowork tab should now be selectable, with "Project or folder" and model options appearing underneath.

docs.title: Quick Checklist
docs.text:
• Windows 11 Pro, Enterprise, or Education (not Home)
  • Paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise)
  • Latest Claude Desktop version
  • Get-Service vmms returns Running
  • Hardware virtualization enabled in BIOS
  • Test-Path C:\Windows\System32\drivers\vfpext.sys returns True
  • Claude Desktop fully quit and relaunched (or reinstalled) after each change

docs.title: Useful Commands Reference
docs.text:
# Check Hyper-V core service
Get-Service vmms

# Enable Hyper-V
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Hyper-V -All

# Enable related features
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Containers -All
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName VirtualMachinePlatform -All

# Check virtualization/firmware status
Get-ComputerInfo -Property "HyperV*"

# Check the vfpext driver file
Test-Path C:\Windows\System32\drivers\vfpext.sys

# Repair Windows servicing components
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
sfc /scannow

Note: If none of the above resolves it, this is a known unresolved issue tracked on Anthropic's GitHub (claude-code repo, e.g. issues #74649, #78858, #78866, #80584, #81396, #80122). Report it through the thumbs-down feedback button in Claude Desktop, referencing "Missing HCS services: vfpext."

docs.title: Managing Your Claude.ai Memory
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

A practical guide to viewing, editing, and controlling what Claude remembers about you.

docs.title: What Is Claude's Memory?
docs.text:
Claude.ai has two memory mechanisms:

  • Auto-generated memory — Claude analyzes your conversation history roughly every 24 hours and synthesizes key context (your job, preferences, projects, etc.) into a memory profile.
  • User-directed edits — Things you explicitly tell Claude to remember or forget. These are stored as discrete entries (up to 30 slots, ~100 characters each).

Note: Memory is scoped separately for regular chats vs. Projects. Information from inside a Project only applies to that Project.

docs.title: Enabling Memory
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings → Capabilities
  2. Toggle on "Generate memory from chat history"
  3. This is the core switch — Claude won't build a memory profile without it.
  4. Optionally enable "Search and reference chats"
  5. This allows Claude to search back through past conversations for relevant details. Useful, but not required for basic memory.

docs.title: Viewing Your Memory
docs.text:
Once Claude has accumulated enough context:

  1. Go to Settings → Capabilities
  2. Click "View and edit memory" in the Memory section
  3. The Manage Memory modal shows everything Claude currently remembers about you

You can also ask Claude directly in any chat:

What do you remember about me?

docs.title: Adding to Memory
docs.text:
Option A — Tell Claude in chat: 

Please remember that I work as a Python programmer.
Remember that I prefer dark mode in all tools.

Option B — Via the memory modal: 1. Open Settings → Capabilities → View and edit memory 2. Click the pencil icon in the lower-left corner of the summary 3. Type the information you want added

Any edits made this way apply immediately to your next conversation.

docs.title: Editing Existing Memory
docs.text:
To update a specific fact: 

Update your memory — I no longer work at Acme Corp, I now work at Example Inc.

To correct something: 

You have my job title wrong. I'm a senior engineer, not a junior engineer.

Claude will use the memory tool to update the entry in place.

docs.title: Deleting / Forgetting Memory
docs.text:
To remove a specific item: 

Please forget that I mentioned my old company.
Forget about my preference for tabs over spaces.

To clear everything: 1. Go to Settings → Capabilities 2. Click "Reset memory" 3. Confirm

Warning: Resetting memory permanently deletes all memories and cannot be undone.

docs.title: Pausing Memory (Without Deleting)
docs.text:
If you want Claude to stop learning new things without wiping existing memory:

  1. Go to Settings → Capabilities
  2. Select "Pause memory"

Claude will retain its current memory but won't add new entries or reference it until you re-enable it.

docs.title: Using Incognito Mode
docs.text:
For conversations you don't want to influence your memory profile at all:

  • Click the ghost icon in the top-right corner of a new chat to enable Incognito mode
  • Incognito chats are never added to memory, regardless of your settings

docs.title: Tips for Getting the Most Out of Memory
docs.text: Do Avoid Reserve explicit edits for stable, permanent facts Burning edit slots on temporary context Use Project knowledge bases for project-specific info Relying on memory across different Projects Periodically review and prune outdated entries Letting old/irrelevant facts accumulate Use Incognito for sensitive or one-off conversations Sharing sensitive info in regular chats

docs.title: Importing Memory from Other AI Providers
docs.text:
If you use ChatGPT, Gemini, or another AI tool:

  1. Go to Settings → Capabilities
  2. Click "Start Import" under Import memory from other AI providers
  3. Claude will generate a prompt you can use to export your context from the other service, then import it

Note: This feature is experimental and still in active development.

For the most up-to-date information, visit support.claude.com

docs.title: Specifying Trusted Cowork Folders
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Trusted Cowork folders let Claude attach a folder to a Cowork task without asking you to confirm each time.

docs.title: Step 1: Open Settings
docs.text: Open the Claude desktop app and go to Settings (the gear icon).

docs.title: Step 2: Go to the Cowork Settings Section
docs.text: In the Settings sidebar, click Cowork. Scroll to Trusted Cowork folders and click Manage.

docs.title: Step 3: Add a Folder
docs.text: The Trusted Cowork folders panel opens, listing any folders already trusted. Click Add folder and choose the folder you want Claude to access without a confirmation prompt.

docs.title: Step 4: Confirm the Folder Was Added
docs.text: The newly added folder appears in the list alongside any existing ones.

docs.title: Step 5: Click Done
docs.text: Click Done to save your changes and close the panel. The folder is now trusted — Claude can attach it to Cowork tasks without asking for confirmation each time.

docs.title: Understanding Cowork and Dispatch
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Claude can operate apps on your computer (browser, spreadsheets, email) to complete tasks while you focus on other things.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Dispatch — Assign tasks from your phone; Claude runs them on your desktop
  • Scheduled tasks — Set recurring tasks (e.g. daily inbox scan, weekly reports)
  • Persistent context — Claude remembers previous work so tasks pick up where they left off
  • No configuration needed — Claude uses connected apps first, then browser or screen

docs.title: How to Get Started
docs.text:
1. Leave your desktop awake
  2. Open Dispatch in Claude Desktop
  3. Pair with the mobile app
  4. Hand off your first task from anywhere

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• These are research previews — complex tasks may need more than one attempt
  • Available on Pro and Max plans only
  • Computer use is limited to macOS — Windows users can use Dispatch but cannot use the full computer control feature yet

Note: Windows users can use Dispatch, but the "Claude operates your screen" feature is not yet available. No release date has been announced.

docs.title: Installing Claude Code on Windows 11
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Claude Code is a command-line coding agent. It runs on Node.js and works well inside VS Code's integrated terminal. This guide walks through installing Node.js, installing Claude Code via npm, and completing first-time setup (theme, login, and trusting your project folder).

docs.title: Part 1: Install Node.js
docs.text: Claude Code requires Node.js. If you don't already have it installed, follow these steps.

docs.title: Step 1: Go to nodejs.org
docs.text: Open nodejs.org in your browser.

docs.title: Step 2: Download the Windows Installer
docs.text: Go to the download page. Choose your Node.js version (LTS recommended), Windows, and download the Windows Installer (.msi).

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Installer
docs.text: Step through the Node.js Setup wizard. On the "Tools for Native Modules" screen, leave the optional Chocolatey/Python/Visual Studio Build Tools checkbox unchecked unless you need to compile native npm modules. Click Next.

docs.title: Step 4: Finish the Install
docs.text: Click Finish once the wizard reports Node.js was installed successfully.

docs.title: Step 5: Open VS Code and a Terminal
docs.text:
Open VS Code, then open a terminal via Terminal → New Terminal.

A new terminal (cmd, in this case) opens at your project path.

docs.title: Step 6: Verify Node.js Is Installed
docs.text:
Run this command to confirm Node.js installed correctly:

node --version

docs.title: Step 7: Install Claude Code Globally via npm
docs.text:
Run:

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

npm installs the package. You may see allow-scripts warnings — these are informational and don't block the install.

Note: If you separately try npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending (as suggested by the warning) and it fails with ENOMATCH / "No installed packages match", don't worry — the Claude Code package itself is still installed correctly. This error only affects optional post-install script approval, not the claude command below.

docs.title: Step 8: Launch Claude Code
docs.text:
Run:

claude

docs.title: Step 9: Choose a Terminal Text Style
docs.text: On first launch, Claude Code asks you to pick a color theme (dark mode, light mode, colorblind-friendly variants, and so on).

docs.title: Step 10: Choose a Login Method
docs.text: Select how you want to authenticate — a Claude subscription (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise), an Anthropic Console account (API billing), or a third-party platform (Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Vertex AI).

docs.title: Step 11: Authorize in the Browser
docs.text:
Claude Code opens your browser to an OAuth authorization page. Review the permissions and click Authorize.

If prompted, sign in again for security before the authorization completes.

docs.title: Step 12: Confirm Login
docs.text: Back in the terminal, Claude Code confirms you're logged in.

docs.title: Step 13: Review the Security Notes
docs.text: Claude Code shows a short security reminder (review Claude's actions, only use it with code you trust). Press Enter to continue.

docs.title: Step 14: Set Up Recommended Terminal Settings
docs.text: Choose Yes, use recommended settings for the optimal coding experience (for example, Shift+Enter for newlines).

docs.title: Step 15: Trust Your Project Folder
docs.text: Claude Code performs a quick safety check on the folder it's about to access. If it's your own project or a trusted one, choose Yes, I trust this folder.

docs.title: Step 16: Confirm Claude Code Is Ready
docs.text: Claude Code is now running and ready for input in your terminal.

docs.title: Part 4 (Optional): VS Code Extension
docs.text: If you're working inside VS Code, Claude Code also installs a companion extension that gives it context on your open and selected files, and lets you review changes inline.

docs.title: Migrating Claude Code from npm to Native Installer
Migrating Claude Code from npm to Native Installer
docs.text: Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text:
When launching Claude Code in VS Code (WSL/Ubuntu), the following message appears in the terminal:

Claude Code has switched from npm to native installer.
Run `claude install` or see https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/getting-started
X Auto-update failed · Try `claude doctor` or `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: Anthropic released a native binary installer for Claude Code in October 2025, replacing the previous npm-based installation. The old npm version detects this and prompts you to migrate. The native installer is simpler, more stable, and does not require Node.js.

docs.title: Step 1: Run the Migration Command
docs.text:
In your terminal (any directory is fine):

claude install

Expected output:

✓ Claude Code successfully installed!

  Version: 2.1.x
  Location: ~/.local/bin/claude

  Next: Run `claude --help` to get started

⚠ Setup notes:
  • Native installation exists but ~/.local/bin is not in your PATH. Run:

  echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc

docs.title: Step 2: Add ~/.local/bin to Your PATH
docs.text:
If the setup notes warn that ~/.local/bin is not in your PATH, run:

echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc

docs.title: Step 3: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
which claude

Expected output:

/home/<username>/.local/bin/claude

If this is correct, the migration is complete.

docs.title: Step 4: Restart VS Code
docs.text: Restart VS Code to ensure all terminals and extensions pick up the new PATH. The warning message should no longer appear.

docs.title: which claude Still Points to an asdf or nvm Shim
docs.text:
If you use a Node.js version manager like asdf or nvm, its shim may still take priority. Uninstall the old npm package from your Node.js versions:

# For asdf
for version in $(asdf list nodejs | tr -d ' *'); do
  echo "Uninstalling from nodejs $version..."
  ASDF_NODEJS_VERSION=$version npm uninstall -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code 2>/dev/null
done

# For nvm
nvm use <version> && npm uninstall -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

Then confirm again:

which claude
# Should now show: /home/<username>/.local/bin/claude

docs.title: General Health Check
docs.text:
claude doctor

This command reports any issues with your installation, such as missing binaries or PATH problems.

docs.title: Setting Up Claude Code in WSL2
Setting Up Claude Code in WSL2
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Set up Claude Code in a WSL2 Ubuntu environment and connect it to an existing MkDocs project.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• WSL2 running Ubuntu
  • VS Code with the Remote – WSL extension installed
  • An existing MkDocs project with a Python venv

docs.title: Step 1: Set Up the Folder Structure
docs.text:
Create a dedicated folder for your Claude Code projects:

mkdir -p ~/projects/<YOUR-FOLDER>/python/mkdocs

The suggested structure is:

~/projects/
└── <YOUR-FOLDER>/
    └── python/
        └── mkdocs/       ← Claude Code project root

docs.title: Step 2: Install Node.js
docs.text:
Claude Code requires Node.js 18 or later. Install it via nvm (Node Version Manager):

curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash

Restart your terminal, then install and activate Node.js:

nvm install --lts
nvm use --lts

Verify the installation:

node --version

docs.title: Step 3: Install Claude Code
docs.text:
Install Claude Code globally via npm:

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

Verify the installation:

claude --version

docs.title: Step 4: First Launch and Authentication
docs.text:
Navigate to your project folder and launch Claude Code:

cd ~/projects/<YOUR-FOLDER>/python/mkdocs
claude

On first launch, Claude Code will prompt you to authenticate:

  1. A browser window opens at claude.ai.
  2. Log in with your Anthropic account.
  3. Copy the authorisation code displayed in the browser.
  4. Paste it back into the terminal prompt.

Claude Code stores the session token locally. You will not need to re-authenticate on subsequent launches.

docs.title: Step 5: Choose How to Use Claude Code
docs.text: There are two ways to run Claude Code depending on your workflow:

docs.title: Option A: VS Code Terminal (Recommended for development)
docs.text:
1. Open VS Code.
  2. Connect to WSL2 via the Remote – WSL extension (F1 → Remote-WSL: New Window).
  3. Open your project folder in VS Code.
  4. Open the integrated terminal (Ctrl+`).
  5. Run claude from the terminal.

Claude Code runs in the same shell as your project, with full access to the filesystem and git history.

docs.title: Option B: Claude Desktop (Recommended for general tasks)
docs.text:
1. Install Claude Desktop on Windows.
  2. Open Claude Desktop and sign in.
  3. Use the built-in Claude Code integration to connect to your WSL2 filesystem.

Use Option B when you want a graphical interface without opening VS Code.

docs.title: Step 6: Recreate the venv After Copying a Project
docs.text:
If you copied or moved the project folder, the existing .venv will have broken absolute paths. Delete it and rebuild:

cd ~/projects/<YOUR-FOLDER>/python/mkdocs
rm -rf .venv

Install python3-venv if it is not already available:

sudo apt install python3-venv

Create a fresh virtual environment and install dependencies:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

(.venv) will appear at the start of your terminal prompt when the environment is active.

docs.title: Step 7: Verify with MkDocs Serve
docs.text:
With the venv active, start the local development server:

mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser. If the site loads correctly, the setup is complete.

To stop the server, press Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Understanding Genspark
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Genspark is a research tool that combines search with AI summarisation. You search as you would with a standard search engine, and the AI organises information from multiple sources into a structured guide page.

For example, searching "Tokyo sightseeing" returns a page already organised into recommended spots, suggested itineraries, and tips — rather than a list of links to browse individually.

docs.title: Applying Nano Banana Prompting Best Practices
Applying Nano Banana Prompting Best Practices
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Official reference: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana

Nano Banana models apply deep reasoning to fully understand your prompt before generating an image. Built on the Gemini 3 family, they support real-time web search, multimodal inputs, multilingual text rendering, and studio-quality visual controls.

docs.title: Core Best Practices
docs.text: Principle Description Be Specific Provide concrete details on subject, lighting, and composition Positive Framing Say "empty street" not "no cars" — describe what you want Control the Camera Use cinematic terms: "low angle," "aerial view," "f/1.8" Iterate Refine with follow-up prompts conversationally

docs.title: 01 — Image Generation
docs.text: Your prompt structure depends on whether you are using reference images or relying solely on text. You are the director — a simple list of keywords won't cut it.

docs.title: Text-to-Image (No References)
docs.text:
Starting from a blank canvas, describe the scene narratively.

Formula:

[Subject] + [Action] + [Location/Context] + [Composition] + [Style]

Example prompt:

A striking fashion model wearing a tailored brown dress, sleek boots, and holding a structured handbag. Posing with a confident, statuesque stance, slightly turned. A seamless, deep cherry red studio backdrop. Medium-full shot, center-framed. Fashion magazine style editorial, shot on medium-format analog film, pronounced grain, high saturation, cinematic lighting effect.

docs.title: Multimodal Generation (With References)
docs.text:
Combine up to 14 reference images in a single prompt — perfect for maintaining character consistency or merging a product into a new environment.

Formula:

[Reference Images] + [Relationship Instruction] + [New Scenario]

Example prompt:

Using the attached napkin sketch as the structure and the attached fabric sample as the texture, transform this into a high-fidelity 3D armchair render. Place it in a sun-drenched, minimalist living room.

docs.title: 02 — Image Editing
docs.text: Editing requires a different mindset. You already have a base image — focus your prompt on what is changing and, critically, what is staying the same.

docs.title: Conversational Editing (No New References)
docs.text:
Generate an image, then tweak it through natural conversation. Semantic masking lets you define a "mask" through text to edit only a specific part of an image.

  • Be explicit about what to keep exactly the same
  • Use clear, direct language for what to remove or change

Example prompt:

"Remove the man from the photo"

docs.title: Composition and Style Transfer (With New References)
docs.text:
Bring new images into the prompt to alter an existing one:

  • Adding elements: Upload a base image + an object image, then tell the model to combine them
  • Style transfer: Upload a photo and ask the model to recreate its content in a different artistic style (e.g., transform a city street into a Van Gogh painting)

docs.title: 03 — Real-Time Information from Web Search
docs.text:
Instead of describing a fictional scene, instruct the model to retrieve real-world data and then specify how to visualize it. Nano Banana 2 is powered by live web search.

Formula:

[Source/Search Request] + [Analytical Task] + [Visual Translation]

Example prompt:

Search for the current weather and date in San Francisco. Analytically, use this data to modify the scene (e.g., if raining, make it look grey and rainy). Visualize this in a miniature city-in-a-cup concept embedded within a realistic, modern smartphone UI.

docs.title: 04 — Text Rendering and Localization
docs.text:
Nano Banana excels at rendering sharp, legible text for posters, diagrams, and product mockups. It supports multilingual text generation in over 10 languages.

Key rules:

  • Enclose desired words in quotes — e.g., "Happy Birthday" or "URBAN EXPLORER"
  • Describe typography style or font name — e.g., "bold, white, sans-serif" or "Century Gothic 12px"
  • Write in one language, specify a different target language for output to localize
  • Text-first hack: First converse with the model to generate text concepts, then ask for an image with that text

Example prompt:

A high-end, glossy commercial beauty shot of a sleek, minimalist nude-colored face moisturizer jar on a warm studio background. Soft, radiant lighting. Render three lines of text: "GLOW" in a flowing Brush Script font; "10% OFF" in a heavy Impact font; "Your First Order" in a thin Century Gothic font. Then translate the text into Korean and Arabic.

docs.title: 05 — Prompting Like a Creative Director
docs.text: Stop typing keywords and start directing the scene. Elevate results from good to breathtaking with four studio-quality controls.

docs.title: Lighting
docs.text:
Tell the model exactly how the scene is illuminated.

Style Example Studio "Three-point softbox setup" Dramatic "Chiaroscuro lighting, harsh high contrast" Natural "Golden hour backlighting, long shadows"

docs.title: Camera, Lens and Focus
docs.text:
Dictate the exact camera type to change the visual DNA of the image.

Camera Effect GoPro Immersive, distorted action feel Fujifilm Authentic color science Disposable Raw, nostalgic flash aesthetic

For lenses: "f/1.8 shallow depth of field" / "wide-angle lens" / "macro lens"

docs.title: Color Grading and Film Stock
docs.text:
The texture and color of the image set the emotional tone.

  • Nostalgic/gritty: "1980s color film, slightly grainy"
  • Modern/moody: "Cinematic color grading, muted teal tones"

docs.title: Materiality and Texture
docs.text:
Define the physical makeup of every element — don't just name it, describe it.

Instead of... Say... "suit jacket" "navy blue tweed jacket" "armor" "ornate elven armor, etched with silver leaf patterns" "coffee mug" "minimalist ceramic coffee mug"

docs.title: Converting a ChatGPT Chat to a Word Document
Converting a ChatGPT Chat to a Word Document
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

This method does not require browser extensions and preserves formatting.

  1. Use the Share feature on the chat.

docs.text: Notes on text-to-speech and voice synthesis tools.

docs.title: Adding CoeiroInk Voices to AivisSpeech
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

coeiroink-v2-bridge is a third-party VVPP plugin that exposes your installed CoeiroInk voices to AivisSpeech through its multi-engine feature — including whichever character voices you already have set up in CoeiroInk.

Prerequisites:

  • AivisSpeech installed
  • CoeiroInk installed, with the voices you want already set up in it
  • Multi-engine function turned on

docs.title: Step 1: Download the Bridge Plugin
docs.text: Go to the coeiroink-v2-bridge GitHub Releases page and download the latest -win.vvpp file.

docs.title: Step 2: Open Manage Voice Synthesis Engines
docs.text: In AivisSpeech, go to 音声合成エンジン (Voice Synthesis Engine) → 音声合成エンジンの管理 (Manage Voice Synthesis Engines).

docs.title: Step 3: Add a New Engine
docs.text: Click ＋追加 (Add) in the top right.

docs.title: Step 4: Select the VVPP File
docs.text:
Stay on the VVPPファイル (VVPP File) tab (the default), then click the folder icon and select the downloaded bridge file.

With the file selected, click ＋追加 (Add).

docs.title: Step 5: Accept the Security Warning
docs.text: Click 追加する (Add) to continue.

docs.title: Step 6: Reload
docs.text: Click 再読み込みする (Reload) to apply the change.

docs.title: Step 7: Restart AivisSpeech
docs.text: Close AivisSpeech completely, just to be safe.

docs.title: Step 8: Launch CoeiroInk
docs.text:
Launch CoeiroInk. AivisSpeech reopens automatically alongside it.

Note: You may see an error saying "VOICEVOX Nemo Engine が異常終了しました" (VOICEVOX Nemo Engine terminated abnormally) at this point. This is a side effect of running multiple engines together, not a problem with the CoeiroInk bridge — click OK and continue.

docs.title: Step 9: Confirm the Voices Are Available
docs.text:
CoeiroInk's own character list shows which voices are installed there.

The same voices now appear in AivisSpeech's character list.

docs.title: Adding a Voice Model from AivisHub
Adding a Voice Model from AivisHub
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

AivisHub is Aivis Project's model-sharing site, where you can browse and install extra voice models — official ones and community-made ones — directly into AivisSpeech.

docs.title: Step 1: Open AivisHub
docs.text:
Create an account on the official site's AivisHub section.

You can also jump straight to AivisHub from inside AivisSpeech: 音声合成モデル (Voice Synthesis Model) → AivisHubで音声合成モデルを探す (Find voice synthesis models on AivisHub).

Either path signs you in and opens your AivisHub dashboard.

docs.title: Step 2: Browse and Filter Models
docs.text:
Click もっと見る (View more) under any category to see its full list.

Narrow the results down with the 掲載区分 (listing type — Official or Community) and 声質 (voice timbre) filters on the left.

docs.title: Step 3: Install the Model
docs.text:
Open a model's page and click 起動中のAivisSpeechにインストール (Install into the running AivisSpeech).

Note: AivisSpeech must already be running for this to work — it installs the model directly into the open instance.

A confirmation message appears once the install finishes.

docs.title: Step 4: Apply the Model in AivisSpeech
docs.text:
Back in AivisSpeech, go to 音声合成モデル (Voice Synthesis Model) → AivisHubで追加した音声合成モデルを反映 (Apply models added on AivisHub).

A confirmation toast appears once it's applied.

docs.title: Step 5: Select the New Model
docs.text: The model now appears at the bottom of the character picker, ready to use like any built-in voice.

docs.text: • AivisHub

docs.title: Adding VOICEVOX Engine to AivisSpeech
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

AivisSpeech's multi-engine feature can load any VOICEVOX API-compatible synthesis engine. This guide adds the official VOICEVOX Engine (plugin build) to AivisSpeech, making VOICEVOX characters like Shikoku Metan and Zundamon available from inside AivisSpeech.

Note: This only works in the VOICEVOX → AivisSpeech direction. Adding an AivisSpeech engine or AIVMX model to VOICEVOX isn't supported, due to compatibility differences.

Prerequisites:

  • AivisSpeech installed
  • Multi-engine function turned on (usually on by default)
  • 7-Zip installed

docs.title: Step 1: Open the VOICEVOX Engine Releases Page
docs.text: Go to the VOICEVOX Engine GitHub Releases page.

docs.title: Step 2: Download the Plugin Engine (VVPP) Build
docs.text:
Scroll to the latest release's パッケージ案内 (Package Guide) section. Under プラグインエンジン（VVPP） (Plugin Engine, VVPP) — not エンジン本体 (Engine itself) — pick the build matching your setup:

  • CPU only → Windows (CPU version)
  • GPU (DirectML) → Windows (GPU/DirectML version)
  • NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) → Windows (GPU/CUDA version) — needs both part1 and part2

Click the link to download (saves as a .7z.001 file).

The download appears in your Downloads folder.

docs.title: Step 3: Extract the Archive
docs.text:
Right-click the downloaded file → 7-Zip → 展開... (Extract...).

Extracting creates a folder containing run.exe, engine_manifest.json, licenses.json, voicevox_core.dll, voicevox_onnxruntime.dll, and the engine_internal, model, and resources folders.

Note: Move this folder somewhere you won't accidentally delete it — e.g. Documents\Voicevox\ — rather than leaving it in Downloads.

docs.title: Step 4: Open Manage Voice Synthesis Engines
docs.text: In AivisSpeech, go to 音声合成エンジン (Voice Synthesis Engine) → 音声合成エンジンの管理 (Manage Voice Synthesis Engines).

docs.title: Step 5: Add a New Engine
docs.text: Click ＋追加 (Add) in the top right.

docs.title: Step 6: Select the Existing Engine Tab
docs.text: Choose the 既存エンジン (Existing Engine) tab — this points AivisSpeech at an already-extracted folder, instead of a single VVPP file.

docs.title: Step 7: Select the Engine Folder
docs.text:
Click the folder icon and select the folder that contains run.exe (e.g. windows-cpu) — select the folder itself, not the run.exe file.

With the folder selected, click ＋追加 (Add).

docs.title: Step 8: Accept the Security Warning
docs.text: AivisSpeech warns that adding an engine could be harmful to your computer, and not to proceed unless you trust the source. Click 追加する (Add) to continue.

docs.title: Step 9: Reload
docs.text: Click 再読み込みする (Reload) to apply the change.

docs.title: Step 10: Confirm It Worked
docs.text:
After reloading, open 音声合成エンジン (Voice Synthesis Engine) again — you should see multiple engines listed (AivisSpeech Engine, VOICEVOX Engine, plus anything else you've added). The character list on the left should now include VOICEVOX characters like Shikoku Metan and Zundamon.

Note: If you already have a single VVPP file instead of an extracted folder, use the VVPPファイル (VVPP File) tab instead of 既存エンジン (Existing Engine).

docs.title: Getting Started with AivisSpeech
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

AivisSpeech is a free Japanese text-to-speech app from the Aivis Project — type text, generate speech, and fine-tune the accent by dragging pitch points.

docs.title: Step 1: Download the Installer
docs.text: Go to the official site and click AivisSpeechをダウンロード (Download AivisSpeech).

docs.title: Step 2: Install AivisSpeech
docs.text: Run the downloaded installer. In Choose Installation Options, select Only for me unless other Windows accounts on the PC also need access.

docs.title: Step 3: Launch AivisSpeech
docs.text: Open AivisSpeech. It starts with a default voice already loaded and an empty text box.

docs.title: Step 4: Generate Speech
docs.text:
Type text into the box, then click Play (▶) in the toolbar to hear it.

Drag the points in the アクセント (Accent) editor at the bottom to adjust the pitch of individual syllables.

docs.title: Step 5: Switch Between Voice Styles
docs.text: Click the character portrait to switch characters or voices. Some characters, like コハク (Kohaku), have several style variations under the same character — Normal, Sweet, Wistful, Sleepy, and so on.

docs.title: Adding a MyCoeiroInk Voice to CoeiroInk
Adding a MyCoeiroInk Voice to CoeiroInk
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

MyCoeiroInk is the community voice library for CoeiroInk, where creators distribute downloadable voice characters. For CoeiroInk's own official character voices instead, see Downloading Built-In Character Voices.

Example voice used: 白痴ー (Hakuchi) One of the most popular male voices on MyCoeiroInk, available in multiple style variations. The voice can also be used as a character called 黒聡 鵜月 (Kurosato Uzuki).

docs.title: Step 1: Download the Voice
docs.text:
1. Go to https://coeiroink.com/mycoeiroink.
  2. Click the center illustration 探す (Sagasu / Search), which navigates to the voice list at https://coeiroink.com/mycoeiroink/list.
  3. Enter 白痴ー (Hakuchi) in the search box and press Enter.
  4. Click the 白痴ー panel in the results — this navigates to the distribution page on BOOTH.
  5. Choose and download a variation as a ZIP file.

Note: 白痴ー (Hakuchi) is distributed as multiple separate ZIP files, each representing a different style:

File name Romaji Style 若輩.zip Jakuhai Inexperienced / junior (kohai) tone Others — Machine-like, Kansai dialect, etc.

If you are unsure where to start, 若輩 (Jakuhai) is a good default.

docs.title: Step 2: Install the Voice into CoeiroInk
docs.text:
1. Extract the ZIP file — inside you will find a folder with an alphanumeric name (e.g. a1b2c3d4...).

  2. Copy that alphanumeric folder into the speaker_info folder inside your CoeiroInk installation directory:

    [CoeiroInk folder]\speaker_info\[alphanumeric folder]

  3. Launch (or restart) CoeiroInk.

  4. Click the character icon at the top of CoeiroInk to open the character dropdown — the new voice should now appear.

docs.title: Step 3: Register the Voice in YMM4
docs.text:
1. In YMM4, go to File → Edit character.
  2. Click the + button at the upper left to create a new character.
  3. Enter a Name (e.g. Kurosato Uzuki).
  4. Set Group to COEIROINK.
  5. Under Voice, click the ↻ (circular arrow icon) next to the voice dropdown.
  6. Select Reload COEIROINK v2 voices — this refreshes the available voice list.
  7. In the Voice dropdown, select COEIROINK2 / 白痴ー.
  8. The Style dropdown will be set automatically if only one style is installed (e.g. 若輩 / Jakuhai). If you have multiple styles installed, select the desired one manually.
  9. Adjust other settings as needed (volume, pitch, speed, intonation, etc.).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Each style variation is a separate download — you can install multiple variations of the same character.
  • If the voice still does not appear after reloading, restart YMM4 and try again.

docs.title: Terms of Use (白痴ー / Hakuchi)
docs.text:
• Commercial and non-commercial use: allowed.
  • Use in ads (games, manga apps, etc.): not allowed.
  • Modifications that closely resemble other existing characters: not allowed.
  • Must comply with CoeiroInk's own terms of use.

docs.title: Downloading Built-In Character Voices
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

CoeiroInk ships with more official character voices than the one or two loaded by default — the rest are downloaded on demand from inside the app. This is separate from MyCoeiroInk, which distributes community-made voices as ZIP files instead.

docs.title: Step 1: Open Character Download
docs.text: Click the character icon, then キャラクターダウンロード (Character Download).

docs.title: Step 2: Read the Notes
docs.text:
A few things worth knowing before downloading:

  • Downloads take effect only after restarting CoeiroInk.
  • Character info must be up to date before you can download a voice model.
  • Each voice model is roughly 364 MB.
  • Downloads can occasionally fail — check the Help page if that happens.
  • User-created voice models are found on MYCOEIROINK instead, not here.

docs.title: Step 3: Update Character Information
docs.text: Find the character you want, then click キャラクター情報の最新化 (Update Character Information).

docs.title: Step 4: Confirm the Update
docs.text: A dialog explains that a new folder will be created under speaker_info, and that the default style downloads along with it. Click 同意して情報の最新化 (Agree and Update Information).

docs.title: Step 5: Download a Style
docs.text: Once the button reads 最新化完了 (Update Complete), click ダウンロード (Download) next to any style you want.

docs.title: Step 6: Restart and Confirm
docs.text: Restart CoeiroInk. The new character now appears in the character dropdown alongside the default one.

CoeiroInk is a free Japanese text-to-speech app. It's portable — no installer, just extract and run.

docs.title: Converting Female Voices to Male Voices
Converting Female Voices to Male Voices
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Use iZotope RX8's Time & Pitch module to shift a female voice toward a more masculine sound by lowering the pitch.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the Audio File
docs.text:
1. Launch iZotope RX8.
  2. Drag and drop a video or audio file onto the application window.
  3. RX8 analyzes the file and opens it in a new tab. Each file gets its own tab — dropping multiple files opens multiple tabs.

docs.title: Step 2: Open Time & Pitch
docs.text:
1. Look at the module list on the right side of the screen.
  2. Click Time & Pitch to open the Time & Pitch dialog.

docs.title: Step 3: Adjust the Pitch
docs.text:
1. Find the Pitch Shift slider or input field.
  2. Set the value to approximately -6 semitones. This shifts the voice down to a more masculine range.

Note: Formant adjustment is still experimental. Changing the formant alongside pitch can improve naturalness, but the optimal settings vary by voice. Try small adjustments and compare results.

docs.title: Step 4: Preview and Compare
docs.text:
1. Click Compare to open the Compare Settings dialog.
  2. To hear the original, select Original audio and click Preview.
  3. To hear your adjusted version, select Time & Pitch: Settings 1 and click Preview.
  4. If you create additional variations, each appears as Settings 2, Settings 3, and so on.

docs.title: Step 5: Remove Unwanted Variations
docs.text:
1. In the Compare Settings dialog, select the variation you want to discard.
  2. Click Remove to delete it from the list.

docs.title: Removing BGM from Audio
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Use iZotope RX8's Music Rebalance module to isolate vocals by removing or reducing background music.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the Audio File
docs.text:
1. Launch iZotope RX8.
  2. Drag and drop an audio file onto the application window.

docs.title: Step 2: Open Music Rebalance
docs.text: 1. In the module list on the right side of the screen, click Music Rebalance.

docs.title: Step 3: Isolate the Vocals
docs.text:
1. To keep only the vocals, lower the faders for all non-vocal elements (bass, drums, other instruments).
  2. Alternatively, click the S (solo) icon on the Vocals fader to mute all other elements at once.

Warning: Do not raise the Vocals fader above its default level. Boosting the vocal volume risks clipping in the output file.

docs.title: Step 4: Set the Quality
docs.text:
• Good (default) — faster processing, suitable for most use cases.
  • Best — higher quality but significantly longer render time.

docs.title: Step 5: Preview and Compare
docs.text:
1. Click Preview to hear your current settings.
  2. Click Compare to open the Compare Settings dialog.
  3. Select Original audio to hear the unprocessed file.
  4. Select Music Rebalance: Settings 1 to hear your adjusted version.

docs.title: Step 6: Export the File
docs.text: 1. When you are satisfied with the result, click Render to export the processed audio file.

docs.title: Removing Vocals from Audio
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Use iZotope RX8's Music Rebalance module to remove or reduce vocals from a track, leaving the instrumental elements intact.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the Audio File
docs.text:
1. Launch iZotope RX8.
  2. Drag and drop an audio file onto the application window.

docs.title: Step 2: Open Music Rebalance
docs.text: 1. In the module list on the right side of the screen, click Music Rebalance.

docs.title: Step 3: Remove the Vocals
docs.text:
1. Lower the Vocals fader to reduce or eliminate the vocal track.
  2. Leave the other faders (bass, drums, other instruments) at their default levels.

docs.title: Step 4: Choose a Processing Mode
docs.text:
Select a mode based on the quality you need:

Mode Quality Processing Time Aggressive Best Longer Gentle Good Faster

docs.title: Step 5: Preview and Compare
docs.text:
1. Click Preview to hear your current settings.
  2. Click Compare to open the Compare Settings dialog.
  3. Select Original audio to hear the unprocessed file.
  4. Select Music Rebalance: Settings 1 to hear your adjusted version.

docs.title: Step 6: Export the File
docs.text:
1. When you are satisfied with the result, click Render.
  2. In the dialog that appears, select your preferred file format and confirm.

docs.title: Stopping Loading Previous Sessions on Startup
Stopping Loading Previous Sessions on Startup
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

When the Load previous session option is enabled, iZotope RX8 saves your work to a session folder and reloads it the next time you launch the application. If you move or delete the original audio files after a session is saved, RX8 displays errors on every startup.

Disabling the option clears all saved session data and prevents RX8 from reloading past work.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the application preferences.
  2. Find the Load previous session checkbox and uncheck it.
  3. RX8 deletes all existing session data immediately.

Note: If you re-enable the checkbox later, RX8 starts saving sessions again from that point onward. Previously deleted session data is not restored.

docs.title: Understanding the Time & Pitch Module
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

The Time & Pitch module adjusts the speed and pitch of audio independently. It is primarily designed for musical material (instruments and vocals) rather than spoken voice, so options for speech processing are limited.

docs.title: Core Parameters
docs.text:
Stretch Ratio Controls playback speed. Lowering the value speeds up the audio; raising it slows it down.

Pitch Shift Controls pitch in semitones. Negative values lower the pitch; positive values raise it.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
Algorithm Best for Radius (best quality) Polyphonic material — instrument mixes, drum loops, rhythmic or non-harmonic audio Solo Instrument Monophonic material — solo strings, human voice Radius RT Polyphonic material where faster processing is needed; slightly lower quality than Radius

Note: Although Solo Instrument is described as suitable for human voice, Radius (best quality) often produces better results in practice. The optimal choice depends on the source material.

docs.title: Advanced Settings
docs.text: Setting Effect on Human Voice Transient sensitivity No noticeable effect Pitch coherence Minimal effect despite the description suggesting otherwise Adaptive window No noticeable effect Noise generation Setting to 0 reduces background noise — the most useful advanced setting for human voice

docs.title: Shift Formants
docs.text:
Formants are the resonance frequency components of a voice and are closely tied to characteristics such as gender and age. Enabling Shift Formants lets you adjust formants independently from pitch and time.

Setting Recommended value Notes Strength 1.0 (default) Higher values may increase perceived volume Shift [Semitones] Varies Negative values lower the voice character; this is the primary setting to adjust for human voice Width Default No noticeable effect on human voice

docs.title: Checking Pinokio Support for Style-Bert-VITS2
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

No official Pinokio script for Style-Bert-VITS2 exists. This page summarizes the current state of Pinokio support and the alternatives available.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:
• Style-Bert-VITS2 does not appear on Pinokio's Discover page.
  • No community-made pinokio.js / install.json scripts for it have been published publicly.

docs.title: Why It Works Fine Without Pinokio
docs.text: Style-Bert-VITS2 already supports a one-click-style installation through bundled .bat scripts. Download the ZIP, extract it, and double-click Install-Style-Bert-VITS2.bat (GPU) or the CPU variant. No Git or Python knowledge is required, which is close to Pinokio's own one-click philosophy. See Set Up Style-Bert-VITS2 WebUI for the full setup process.

docs.title: Options if You Still Want Pinokio
docs.text:
• Use the .bat installer directly: This is the officially recommended path, and arguably simpler than Pinokio for this tool.
  • Write your own Pinokio script: Any GitHub repository with a pinokio.js plus install.js / start.js scripts can be installed through Pinokio. You can write these scripts to clone the Style-Bert-VITS2 repository and run the equivalent of the .bat steps with shell.run.
  • Use it as a Python library: For synthesis-only use, Style-Bert-VITS2 is published as a pip package (pip install style-bert-vits2) and runs on CPU without an NVIDIA GPU. This suits integration scenarios, such as connecting to YMM4 through its API, more than a standalone WebUI setup.

docs.title: Setting Up Style-Bert-VITS2 WebUI
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Style-Bert-VITS2 is a free, open-source text-to-speech engine that supports Japanese, English, and Chinese. It runs locally on your PC and can be connected to YMM4 as a voice engine.

docs.title: What is Style-Bert-VITS2?
docs.text:
• Developed by litagin02, based on the original Bert-VITS2 project
  • Not YMM4-specific — it is a general-purpose TTS engine
  • Connects to YMM4 via a local API server (similar to VOICEVOX and CoeiroInk)
  • Supports multiple languages including English with the right voice model
Bert-VITS2 (original)
    └── Style-Bert-VITS2 (litagin02's fork, adds style control)
            └── AivisSpeech (uses Style-Bert-VITS2 as its engine)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10/11
  • Python 3.12.x
  • ~5 GB free disk space (for models and dependencies)
  • NVIDIA GPU recommended but not required (CPU works for inference)

docs.title: Step 1: Download Style-Bert-VITS2
docs.text:
1. Go to the Style-Bert-VITS2 GitHub repository.
  2. Click the green Code button → Download ZIP.
  3. Extract to a folder with no Japanese characters or spaces in the path.

Warning: The path must not contain Japanese characters or spaces. Example of a valid path: D:\00-portable-apps\Style-Bert-VITS2-master

docs.title: Step 2: Set Up the Virtual Environment
docs.text:
Open a terminal in the extracted folder and run the following commands one by one.

Create the venv:

python -m venv venv

Activate the venv:

venv\Scripts\activate

You should see (venv) at the start of your prompt.

Verify Python version:

python --version

Python 3.12.x is recommended.

docs.title: Step 3: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
This version of Style-Bert-VITS2 includes requirements-infer.txt for inference-only use (lighter than the full requirements.txt, which includes training tools).

Install inference dependencies:

pip install -r requirements-infer.txt

Note: This will take several minutes as it downloads PyTorch and other large packages.

Upgrade PyTorch to the latest version (required — the version pinned in requirements-infer.txt is too old):

pip install torch torchaudio --upgrade

Upgrade pip (optional but recommended):

python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip

docs.title: Step 4: Initialize (Download Models)
docs.text:
Run initialize.py with the --only_infer flag to skip downloading heavy training models:

python initialize.py --only_infer

This downloads:

  • BERT language models (including English deberta-v3-large)
  • Default Japanese voice models (jvnv-F1-jp, jvnv-F2-jp, jvnv-M1-jp, jvnv-M2-jp, koharune-ami, amitaro)

Note: The script may complete silently with no output — this is normal. Verify by checking that the bert\ and model_assets\ folders were created and populated.

docs.title: Step 5: Launch the WebUI
docs.text:
python app.py

The WebUI will open automatically in your browser at http://127.0.0.1:7860.

Note: To launch in future sessions, activate the venv first, then run python app.py: 

venv\Scripts\activate
python app.py

docs.title: WebUI Overview
docs.text: Element Japanese Romaji Description Model list モデル一覧 Moderu ichiran Select a voice model Load button ロード Rōdo Load the selected model Text input テキスト Tekisuto Enter text to synthesize Language Language — Select JP / EN / ZH Synthesize button 音声合成 Onsei gōsei Generate the voice Style スタイル Sutairu Emotional style of the voice

docs.title: Default Voice Models
docs.text:
Model Type jvnv-F1-jp Japanese female 1 jvnv-F2-jp Japanese female 2 jvnv-M1-jp Japanese male 1 jvnv-M2-jp Japanese male 2 koharune-ami Japanese female (Koharune Ami) amitaro Japanese female (Amitaro)

Note: The default models are Japanese only. To use native English TTS, an English-trained model such as the RikkaBotan model must be added separately.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Keep the terminal window open while using the WebUI — closing it stops the server.
  • The venv must be activated each session before launching.
  • The PyTorch upgrade (pip install torch torchaudio --upgrade) is required due to a version conflict with the transformers library.

docs.title: Stopping Style-Bert-VITS2 WebUI
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Follow these steps to shut down the Style-Bert-VITS2 WebUI server cleanly. See Set Up Style-Bert-VITS2 WebUI for how to launch it.

docs.title: Step 1: Stop the Server
docs.text: In the terminal running the server, press Ctrl + C to stop app.py.

docs.title: Step 2: Exit the Virtual Environment
docs.text:
Run the following command to deactivate the venv:

deactivate

Note: Closing the terminal window also stops the server, but running deactivate first leaves your shell in a clean state for the next session.

docs.title: Fixing a MeCab Initialization Error
docs.text: Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
Generating speech with a Japanese voice on the Kokoro 82M engine can fail with:

Generation failed
Failed initializing MeCab. Please see the README for possible solutions:
https://github.com/polm/fugashi
If you are still having trouble here, and include the ERROR DETAILS below:
https://github.com/polm/fugashi/issues
------------------- ERROR DETAILS -------------------
...
param.cpp(69) [ifs] no such file or directory: C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\Temp\_MEI######\unidic\dicdir\...

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: Voicebox uses fugashi, a Python wrapper around the MeCab Japanese tokenizer, to process Japanese text before synthesis. Per fugashi's README, MeCab always needs a dictionary to run — it can't tokenize anything without one. The no such file or directory line points straight at the dictionary path it expected (unidic\dicdir) inside _MEI######, a temporary folder that PyInstaller-packaged apps like Voicebox extract themselves into at launch. That folder is missing the UniDic dictionary files MeCab needs.

docs.title: What Fugashi's README Says
docs.text:
For a normal Python install, fugashi's own fix is to install a dictionary package:

Option Command Quick start (smaller) pip install 'fugashi[unidic-lite]' Full dictionary pip install 'fugashi[unidic]' then python -m unidic download

Note: These are pip commands for a Python environment you control. Voicebox is a self-contained Windows app, not something you pip install into, so this isn't a fix you can run yourself. It's included here to explain why the error happens, not as a direct solution.

docs.title: What You Can Try
docs.text:
• Restart Voicebox and generate again. The _MEI###### folder name changes on every launch — if the dictionary files failed to extract because of a one-off glitch (antivirus interference, a locked file), a clean relaunch may extract them successfully.
  • Reinstall Voicebox. If the dictionary was never bundled into your installed copy correctly, restarting won't help — reinstalling the latest version should re-extract the full package contents.
  • Stick to English voices (either engine) if the above doesn't work. English generation doesn't depend on MeCab at all — it's Japanese-specific.
  • Report the error upstream. If it persists after a reinstall, this looks like a Voicebox packaging bug — the dictionary genuinely isn't shipping inside the executable — rather than something fixable on the fugashi/MeCab side. File it with the full ERROR DETAILS block from the popup.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• fugashi (GitHub) — the library Voicebox uses for Japanese tokenization
  • Voicebox (GitHub) — search or file an issue here if a reinstall doesn't fix it; Voicebox's Python backend (where this error originates) is PyInstaller-bundled, matching the _MEI###### temp path in the error
  • Voicebox DeepWiki — ask the AI documentation assistant about how Voicebox bundles its Python backend
  • Using a Preset Voice — where this error was first encountered, using the Kumo Kokoro 82M voice

docs.title: Understanding Voicebox
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Voicebox is a voice cloning tool that generates speech in your own voice from a short recording. It is not the same as VOICEVOX (the Japanese TTS software).

  • Uses Alibaba's Qwen3 TTS audio AI model
  • Free and runs locally — no cloud required
  • Works as a Windows app without Python

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Launch the app.
  2. On first run, download the Qwen3 TTS model.
  3. Record a few seconds of your voice with a microphone.
  4. Create a voice profile.
  5. Enter text to generate speech in your voice.

docs.title: Audio Quality
docs.text:
• Relatively natural with good intonation
  • Pauses naturally at full stops
  • May mispronounce some words — review output before use

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• GPU recommended (e.g. RTX 4070 Ti generates ~17 seconds of audio in ~3 minutes)
  • Generation-based, not real-time

docs.title: Pros
docs.text:
• Completely free
  • Local processing (private)
  • Voice cloning from a short sample
  • Easy setup

docs.title: Cons
docs.text:
• Slow generation
  • Occasional mispronunciation
  • High-end GPU recommended for comfort
  • Risk of misuse for voice deepfakes

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Narration
  • Video and streaming content
  • AI voice content
  • VTuber voices

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• Official site
  • GitHub repository (jamiepine/voicebox) — open-source; a Tauri (Rust) shell around a React frontend and a PyInstaller-bundled FastAPI Python backend
  • DeepWiki AI documentation — ask questions about the codebase directly
  • Madosoft review (Impress)

docs.title: Using a Preset Voice
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Voicebox also ships with a small set of built-in preset voices, so you can generate speech without recording your own voice sample first.

docs.title: Step 1: Open Create Voice
docs.text: Click Create Voice.

docs.title: Step 2: Choose a Built-In Voice
docs.text: In the Create Voice dialog, click Built-in voice instead of Clone from audio.

docs.title: Step 3: Pick an Engine
docs.text: Preset voices are only available for two engines: Kokoro 82M and Qwen CustomVoice.

docs.title: Step 4: Browse the Available Voices
docs.text:
Scroll through the Voice list to see what each engine offers. Kokoro 82M's list is mostly English (en) voices:

Scroll further down for the Japanese (ja) voices — there aren't many, and Kumo is the only male one:

Qwen CustomVoice has even fewer voices: two English (Ryan, Aiden) and one Japanese (Ono Anna).

docs.title: Step 5: Create the Voice Profile
docs.text:
Select a voice, name the profile, set its language, then click Create Profile. For example, selecting Ryan and naming it ryan-male-en:

The new profile appears as a card, and the generate bar at the bottom defaults to it.

docs.title: Step 6: Generate Speech
docs.text:
With the profile selected, type text into the box at the bottom and click the generate button.

Generation takes a moment — Voicebox shows a "Loading model..." status while it works.

docs.title: Step 7: Play the Result
docs.text: Once it finishes, a waveform player appears so you can listen right away.

docs.title: Step 8: Favorite, Export, or Delete a Generation
docs.text:
Click the star on a generation to mark it as a favorite.

Open its ... menu to play it again, export the audio or a full package, apply effects, regenerate, or delete it.

docs.title: Managing Voice Profiles
docs.text:
The microphone icon in the sidebar opens the Voices page, where you can view and edit every profile in more detail — description, language, default effects, and audio samples.

Warning: Voice profile selection is filtered by engine — a profile made with one engine (e.g. Qwen CustomVoice) can't be selected while a different engine (e.g. Kokoro 82M) is active, and vice versa. Voicebox shows "Only supported voice profiles can be selected for the current model" when this happens.

For example, creating a second profile from Kokoro 82M's Kumo voice, named kumo-male-ja in Japanese:

Both profiles now show up in the Voices list.

Back on the main page, selecting kumo-male-ja grays out ryan-male-en (different engine), and the generate bar switches to Japanese and Kokoro 82M automatically.

Warning: Generating with a Japanese Kokoro 82M voice may fail with a Failed initializing MeCab error. This is a missing dependency in Voicebox itself, not a mistake in your setup — see Fixing a MeCab Initialization Error for details.

docs.title: Accessing VOICEVOX's GitHub Repositories
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

VOICEVOX is split across separate repositories — the Engine (an HTTP server) and the Core (the speech synthesis library) are both linked from the official site, for anyone who wants to build on VOICEVOX instead of just using the desktop app.

docs.title: VOICEVOX Engine
docs.text: VOICEVOX Engine is the HTTP server VOICEVOX itself runs on — send it a request and it returns synthesized speech.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the Official Site
docs.text: Go to the official VOICEVOX site, scroll down to the 音声合成エンジン (Voice Synthesis Engine) section, then click VOICEVOX ENGINE.

docs.title: Step 2: Open the GitHub Repository
docs.text: This opens the VOICEVOX/voicevox_engine GitHub repository, with links to the User Guide, Contributor Guide, and Developer Guide depending on what you want to do.

docs.title: VOICEVOX Core
docs.text: VOICEVOX Core is the underlying speech synthesis library — a lower-level building block than the Engine, distributed as a C API (.so/.dll/.dylib) or a Python API (.whl).

docs.title: Step 1: Open the Official Site
docs.text: Scroll further down to the コアライブラリ (Core Library) section, then click VOICEVOX CORE.

docs.title: Step 2: Open the GitHub Repository
docs.text: This opens the VOICEVOX/voicevox_core GitHub repository. Releases has prebuilt libraries for both APIs, plus sample execution instructions for Python and C++ (CMake or Visual Studio).

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
• VOICEVOX Engine (GitHub)
  • VOICEVOX Core (GitHub)
  • VOICEVOX Editor (GitHub) — the desktop app itself

docs.title: Adding AivisSpeech Engine to VOICEVOX
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

This isn't supported. AivisSpeech's engine and AIVMX voice models can't be added to VOICEVOX — only the VOICEVOX → AivisSpeech direction works, due to compatibility differences.

To bring VOICEVOX characters into AivisSpeech instead, see Adding VOICEVOX Engine to AivisSpeech.

docs.title: Adding Nemo Voices
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

VOICEVOX Nemo is a free, character-less voice library — extra voices (numbered, not named) you can add to VOICEVOX as a separate multi-engine.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the Official Site
docs.text: Go to the official VOICEVOX site.

docs.title: Step 2: Open VOICEVOX Nemo
docs.text: Scroll down and click VOICEVOX Nemo.

docs.title: Step 3: Open the Nemo Download Page
docs.text: On the VOICEVOX Nemo page, click ダウンロード (Download).

docs.title: Step 4: Review the Setup Steps
docs.text:
A usage guide dialog appears with three steps: install VOICEVOX, turn on the Multi-engine function in VOICEVOX's settings, then download the Nemo Engine. Click Nemo エンジン ダウンロード (Nemo Engine Download) — Step 3 in the dialog.

Note: Skip Step 1 in the dialog (installing VOICEVOX) if you already have it installed.

docs.title: Step 5: Open Options
docs.text: In VOICEVOX, go to 設定 (Settings) → オプション (Options).

docs.title: Step 6: Turn On the Multi-Engine Function
docs.text: Under 高度な設定 (Advanced Settings), turn on マルチエンジン機能 (Multi-engine function).

docs.title: Step 7: Download the Nemo Engine
docs.text:
Back on the download dialog, choose your OS and mode (GPU/CPU or CPU-only), then click ダウンロード (Download).

Warning: If AivisSpeech is also installed, double-clicking the downloaded .vvpp file may launch AivisSpeech instead of VOICEVOX and import the Nemo voices there — as extra numbered character slots — rather than into VOICEVOX. If that happens, skip ahead and add the engine to VOICEVOX manually using Steps 8–12 below.

docs.title: Step 8: Open Manage Engines
docs.text: In VOICEVOX, go to エンジン (Engine) → エンジンの管理 (Manage Engines).

docs.title: Step 9: Add a New Engine
docs.text: Click 追加 (Add).

docs.title: Step 10: Select the VVPP File
docs.text: Choose the VVPPファイル (VVPP File) tab, select the downloaded .vvpp file, then click 追加 (Add).

docs.title: Step 11: Reload
docs.text: Click 再読み込みする (Reload) to apply the new engine.

docs.title: Step 12: Confirm the Nemo Voices Are Added
docs.text: The new Nemo voices — six female (女声1–6) and three male (男声1–3) — appear in the character list, marked NEW!.

docs.title: Installing VOICEVOX

VOICEVOX is a free, open-source text-to-speech application for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

You will be asked: "Who should this application be installed for?"

Option When to choose Only for me (recommended) Personal use on your own Windows account. No admin rights needed. Anyone who uses this computer Only if multiple Windows users need access to VOICEVOX. Requires admin rights.

docs.title: Fixing "Failed to Connect to the Docker API" in VS Code
Fixing "Failed to Connect to the Docker API" in VS Code
Environment
docs.text:
• OS: Windows 11
  • Subsystem: WSL2 (Ubuntu)
  • Editor: Visual Studio Code
  • VS Code Extension: WSL
  • Docker: Docker Desktop

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
Running the following command in the Ubuntu terminal inside VS Code:

terminal
docker run --rm -it -p 8000:8000 -v $(pwd):/mkdocs mkdocs-dev

Results in:

terminal
failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock; 
check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running: 
dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: connect: no such file or directory

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: Docker Desktop is running, but WSL integration for the Ubuntu distro is disabled. As a result, the Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) is not available inside WSL.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Open Docker Desktop.

  2. Go to Settings.

  3. Navigate to Resource → WSL integration.

    1. Enable:
      • Enable integration with my default WSL distro.
      • Ubuntu under Enable integration with additional distros.
    2. Click Apply & restart.

  4. Restart VS Code.

docs.title: Fixing WSL Integration Unexpectedly Stopped in Docker Desktop
Fixing WSL Integration Unexpectedly Stopped in Docker Desktop
docs.text: Restart WSL integration for your Linux distribution in Docker Desktop.

docs.title: Method 1: Restart WSL Integration from the Prompt
docs.text:
1. When the error dialog appears, click Restart the WSL integration.

  2. Wait for Docker Desktop to restart the integration.

docs.title: Method 2: Re-enable WSL Integration from Settings
docs.text:
1. Click Skip WSL distro integration.

  2. Open Docker Desktop.

  3. Click Settings (gear icon).

  4. Go to Resources → WSL integration.

  5. Enable:

    • Enable integration with my default WSL distro
    • Your distribution (for example, Ubuntu)

  6. Click Apply & restart.

  7. Wait for Docker Desktop to restart.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Open a WSL terminal and run:

docker version

Confirm that Docker responds without errors.

docs.title: Note
docs.text:
If integration repeatedly stops:

  • Restart WSL:
wsl --shutdown

  • Then reopen Docker Desktop.

  • Ensure your WSL distribution is running:

wsl -l -v

docs.title: Installing Python Packages with pip in Docker
Installing Python Packages with pip in Docker
docs.text: Install MkDocs and related plugins inside a Docker image using requirements.txt.

docs.title: What this guide does
docs.text:
• Explains how pip install works inside Docker
  • Shows the correct Dockerfile setup
  • Explains when you must rebuild the image
  • Prevents common dependency issues

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create or update requirements.txt.

    mkdocs<2
mkdocs-material
mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin
mkdocs-static-i18n
mkdocs-glightbox

    Add or remove packages as needed.

  2. Install dependencies during Docker build.

    In your Dockerfile, include:

    FROM python:3.12-slim

RUN apt-get update \
&& apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git \
&& rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN git config --system --add safe.directory /mkdocs

WORKDIR /mkdocs

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["mkdocs", "serve", "-a", "0.0.0.0:8000"]

    Important:

    • COPY requirements.txt . happens before copying the whole project.
    • pip install runs during build, not during docker run.

  3. Build the image.

    docker build -t my-mkdocs .

    If you changed requirements.txt, use:

    docker build --no-cache -t my-mkdocs .

  4. Run the container.

    docker run --rm -it -p 8000:8000 -v $(pwd):/mkdocs my-mkdocs

docs.title: pip install does NOT run during docker run
docs.text:
This command:

docker run ...

does not install packages.

All Python dependencies must already be installed during:

docker build

docs.title: When you must rebuild
docs.text:
Rebuild if you change:

  • requirements.txt
  • Dockerfile
  • Python version in FROM python:...

You do not need to rebuild for:

  • Markdown changes
  • CSS changes
  • HTML override changes
  • mkdocs.yml changes

docs.title: Optional: Verify installed packages
docs.text:
Run:

docker run --rm -it my-mkdocs pip list

Or check MkDocs version:

docker run --rm -it my-mkdocs mkdocs --version

docs.title: Why this pattern is recommended
docs.text:
This order:

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .

improves build caching.

Docker only re-installs dependencies when requirements.txt changes.

Content edits do not trigger re-installation.

This setup ensures:

  • Clean dependency management
  • Reproducible builds
  • Correct behavior in Docker + GitHub Actions
  • Stable MkDocs 1.x environment

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
Running the following command in the Ubuntu terminal inside VS Code:

git commit -m "Initial MkDocs site"

results in the following message:

Author identity unknown

*** Please tell me who you are.

Run

  git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
  git config --global user.name "Your Name"

to set your account's default identity.
Omit --global to set the identity only in this repository.

fatal: empty ident name (for <kuroraiun@Daiv-001.localdomain>) not allowed

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:

docs.title: Understanding Inno Setup
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Inno Setup is a free, open-source installer creation tool for Windows, originally developed by Jordan Russell. It packages an application — including all its files, dependencies, and settings — into a single .exe installer that end users can run to install the software.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Script-based configuration — Installers are defined using .iss script files (Pascal-based syntax), giving fine-grained control over the installation process.
  • Single-file output — Produces a compact, self-contained .exe installer.
  • Customizable UI — The installation wizard's appearance, steps, and dialogs can be customized.
  • Registry and shortcut support — Can write to the Windows Registry, create Start Menu shortcuts, and set environment variables.
  • Uninstaller generation — Automatically generates an uninstaller.
  • Unicode support — Supports multilingual installers.
  • Free to use — No cost, even for commercial projects.

docs.title: Use with PyInstaller
docs.text:
A common workflow for distributing Python desktop apps to Windows users is:

  1. Use PyInstaller to convert a Python script into a standalone .exe with all its dependencies.
  2. Use Inno Setup to package the PyInstaller output folder into a polished Windows installer with install/uninstall support.

See Create an Installer for a Python App for the full workflow.
