docs.title: Charging and Reverse Charging
docs.text: Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

docs.title: Charge the Tablet
docs.text:
There are three ways to charge the tablet:

  1. Official charger (preferred): Use the standard charger plug and data cable included with the tablet.
  2. Third-party charger: Use a charger plug and data cable from another tablet or phone brand. Preferred specifications: 9V2A or 5V3A.

  3. PC charging via USB:

    1. Connect the tablet to the PC with a Type-C cable (a USB adapter may be required).
    2. On the tablet, select Charge the device from the pop-up window.

Note: Charge the tablet with the screen off when possible — charging while the screen is on extends the charging time. Use the official charger when available.

docs.title: Charge Another Phone in Reverse
docs.text:
The tablet has an 8000 mAh battery when fully charged. You can use it to temporarily charge an Android phone.

  1. Connect the tablet to the Android phone using a USB-C to USB-C cable.
  2. On the tablet, select Use as power supply from the pop-up window.

Note: Reverse charging supports Android phones only — not iOS devices. The output is approximately 2W, which is suitable for emergency use but not for everyday charging.

docs.title: Comparing Pen Display Apps for the Magic Drawing Pad
Comparing Pen Display Apps for the Magic Drawing Pad
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Several apps let you use the Magic Drawing Pad as a wireless pen display on Windows 11. They fall into two categories: display extension apps and remote desktop apps. For Blender's pressure-sensitive tools, only SpaceDesk, SuperDisplay, and Duet Display are practical on Windows — Weylus's pressure and tilt support is Linux-only, and remote desktop apps generally do not pass pressure through either.

docs.title: Display Extension Apps
docs.text:
These apps add the tablet as an extra Windows monitor. The stylus works as pen input on that display.

App Price Strength Limitation SpaceDesk Free Broad device support Pen experience varies; may need tweaking SuperDisplay Paid Polished pen experience for artists Focused on drawing; less general-purpose Duet Display Paid Reliable, low latency Subscription-based Weylus Free & open source No account required; works through any browser Pressure and tilt require a Linux host — on Windows 11 it only provides pointer and touch, not usable for Blender's pressure-sensitive tools

docs.title: Remote Desktop Apps
docs.text:
These apps stream the entire Windows desktop to the tablet as a video feed. The tablet does not appear as a second monitor in Windows — it shows a mirrored or remote view of the existing display.

App Pen Pressure for Blender Chrome Remote Desktop Not supported — stylus input is treated as mouse clicks Microsoft Remote Desktop Not supported — same limitation; designed for remote access, not display extension Sunshine + Moonlight Not yet verified — low-latency, GPU-encoded game streaming, but pressure passthrough for apps like Blender has not been confirmed

Blender relies on pressure-sensitive stylus input for sculpting and texture painting. Chrome Remote Desktop and Microsoft Remote Desktop do not pass stylus pressure data through, making them unsuitable for this workflow. Sunshine and Moonlight are architecturally similar but untested for pressure support — see Connecting Wirelessly for setup steps if you want to try it.

docs.title: Set Up Weylus
docs.text:
Note: Weylus's pressure and tilt support requires a Linux host. On Windows 11, Weylus only provides pointer and touch control — it will not give you pressure-sensitive input in Blender.

  1. Download Weylus for Windows from GitHub.
  2. Install the Weylus virtual input driver: the setup wizard guides you through installing vJoy, which lets Weylus send pointer and touch input to Windows.
  3. Run Weylus on your PC. It displays a local URL such as 192.168.x.x:8001 and a QR code.
  4. Open a web browser on your tablet, enter the URL, and your PC screen appears.
  5. In the Weylus browser interface on your tablet, check Capture Stylus to use the stylus as a pointer. The Pressure Sensitivity option has no effect on Windows.

docs.title: Why SpaceDesk
docs.text:
SpaceDesk works well when:

  • You already have a large Android drawing tablet and want to use it without extra cost.
  • Your PC and tablet are on the same local network.
  • You need an extra monitor with pen input for Blender rather than a dedicated drawing workspace.
  • The use case does not require a professional or portable studio setup.

For Blender work in particular, having the tablet as an additional display with stylus input is enough for most workflows. SpaceDesk provides this at no cost.

docs.title: Connecting by Cable
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

The Magic Drawing Pad supports DisplayPort Alt Mode over its USB-C port, so it can act as a wired pen display with no app or Wi-Fi required.

Note: Your PC needs a USB-C port that supports DisplayPort output (DP Alt Mode) — not every USB-C port does.

  1. Connect the Magic Drawing Pad to your PC using the provided cable.
  2. Press the DP-IN button shown on the tablet's screen.

The tablet switches to display the PC's output directly, with no separate viewer app needed.

Note: See this video for a demonstration of the wired setup.

docs.title: Connecting Wirelessly
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

Two apps let you use the Magic Drawing Pad as a wireless screen for Windows over Wi-Fi: SpaceDesk, which adds the tablet as an extra monitor, and Sunshine and Moonlight, which streams your existing desktop to the tablet as a video feed. Both your PC and the Magic Drawing Pad must be on the same Wi-Fi network.

docs.title: Method 1: SpaceDesk (Extra Monitor)
docs.text: SpaceDesk is a free, unofficial third-party app that turns the Magic Drawing Pad into a wireless pen display for Windows. The tablet appears as an additional monitor, and the stylus works as a pen input device.

docs.title: On Windows
docs.text:
1. Go to spacedesk.net/download/.
  2. Download the SpaceDesk Driver for Windows.
  3. Run the installer and follow the prompts.
  4. Open the SpaceDesk Driver Console and confirm the driver is on.

docs.title: On the Magic Drawing Pad
docs.text:
1. Open the Google Play Store.
  2. Search for SpaceDesk.
  3. Install the SpaceDesk VIEWER app.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: State Effect on Windows SpaceDesk Viewer connected Tablet appears as an extra monitor Viewer disconnected or closed Extra monitor disappears from Windows Driver turned off No new connections can be established

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Open the SpaceDesk Driver Console on Windows and turn the driver on.
  2. Open the SpaceDesk Viewer app on the Magic Drawing Pad.
  3. Tap your PC in the list.

Windows adds the tablet as an extra monitor.

docs.title: Disconnect
docs.text:
1. Swipe away the SpaceDesk Viewer app on the Magic Drawing Pad, or disconnect from inside the app.
  2. Open the SpaceDesk Driver Console on Windows and turn the driver off.

The session has ended when Windows Display Settings no longer shows the tablet as a monitor.

Note: If Windows gets confused about monitor arrangement after reconnecting, open Display Settings and drag the monitors back into the correct positions. Windows sometimes places a reconnected monitor in an unexpected location.

docs.title: Method 2: Sunshine and Moonlight (Screen Mirroring)
docs.text:
Sunshine (host, on your PC) and Moonlight (client, on the Magic Drawing Pad) stream your Windows desktop using your GPU's hardware encoder for low latency. Unlike SpaceDesk, the tablet does not appear as a new Windows monitor — it shows a mirrored, remote view of your existing desktop instead.

For the full installation, pairing, and streaming steps, see Streaming a Windows PC to an Android Tablet with Sunshine and Moonlight.

Note: Pen pressure through this method has not been verified for apps like Blender. See that guide's Known Limitations section for details.

docs.title: Powering On, Off, and Restarting
docs.text: Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

docs.title: Power On
docs.text: Press and hold the power button for about 5 seconds. Release the button when the XPPen startup screen appears.

docs.title: Shut Down or Restart
docs.text:
Hold the power button for about 2 seconds. When the prompt page appears, select Power off or Restart.

Note: Restart the tablet regularly to clear the running cache and keep it in good condition. If the tablet is not working properly, try restarting it first.

docs.title: Force Shutdown
docs.text: If the device is unresponsive and cannot be restored by restarting, hold the power button for more than 10 seconds to force a shutdown.

docs.title: Preventing Finger False Touch
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

The Magic Drawing Pad supports both hand touch and pen touch. By default, the system gives priority to pen touch: when the stylus is detected, finger input is ignored.

There are two additional ways to prevent accidental finger touches while drawing.

docs.title: Method 1: Use the Included Glove
docs.text: The package includes a glove designed for use while painting. Wearing it on your drawing hand prevents accidental finger touches.

docs.title: Method 2: Disable Handwriting Touch
docs.text:
Disabling handwriting touch lets you draw with the stylus without any risk of finger input being registered. There are two ways to toggle this setting:

  • Shortcut menu: Pull down the shortcut menu from the top of the screen and tap the Handwriting Touch switch.
  • Settings: Go to Settings → Advanced Features → Handwriting Touch and toggle it off.

docs.title: Redeeming ibis Paint X Membership
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

XPPen Magic Drawing Pad owners can redeem a free ibis Paint X membership using a code obtained from the XPPen website.

Note: ibis Paint X must be version V11.1.1 or later. Update the app on Google Play if needed.

docs.title: Step 1: Get a Membership Code
docs.text: Open the XPPen free drawing software page, select ibis Paint X, and go to the details page. Register an XPPen account as prompted, enter your device serial number and other required information, and receive your membership code.

docs.title: Step 2: Open the Redemption Screen
docs.text: On the tablet, open ibis Paint X. Tap the Settings button in the upper-right corner, scroll down to find Additional Features, and tap Use Membership Code.

docs.title: Step 3: Create or Log In to an ibis Account
docs.text:
If you do not have an ibis account, tap Don't have an account yet? to register.

Enter your email, password, and nickname. Check the box to agree to the Terms of Service, complete any verification, and tap Create.

If you already have an ibis account, log in directly and skip to Step 4.

docs.title: Step 4: Redeem the Code
docs.text:
Log in to your ibis Paint X account.

Enter the membership code from Step 1 and tap Redeem. A pop-up window confirms the redemption was successful.

docs.title: Transferring Files to a PC
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

You can transfer or sync files between the tablet and a PC using a wired or wireless connection.

docs.title: Method 1: Wired (USB 2.0 OTG)
docs.text:
1. Connect the tablet to the PC with a USB cable.

  2. On the tablet, choose the mode from the pop-up window: Transfer file or Transfer picture.

  3. On the PC (Windows or Mac), open File Explorer or Finder. The tablet appears as a disk directory folder.

    Windows file directory:

    Mac OS file directory:

Note: Mac computers require the "Android File Transfer" app to be installed first. Computers running Windows XP may not connect properly — install Windows Media Player 11 or later if needed.

docs.title: Method 2: Bluetooth Wireless
docs.text:
Bluetooth file transfer supports Android devices to Windows PCs only. It does not support iOS phones or macOS devices.

  1. Turn on Bluetooth on both the tablet and the PC.
  2. On the Windows PC, open the Bluetooth settings and click Receive File to enter the receiving state.

  3. On the tablet, select the file to transfer and choose Bluetooth to share it.

  4. Select the PC from the list of Bluetooth devices.

  5. On the PC, accept the file and choose a save path. The transfer is complete.

docs.title: Understanding the Home Screen
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

The XPPen Magic Drawing Pad home screen has a simple design for faster operation and a more personalized interface.

Top status bar: Displays the drawing pad status and notification messages.

Bottom Favorites bar: Holds frequently used apps that you can remove or replace.

docs.title: Desktop Settings
docs.text:
To access desktop settings (wallpapers, themes, micro-components, and more), tap and hold a blank area of the home screen. This opens the desktop Settings interface.

You can also configure home screen settings through the main Settings app.

docs.title: Using the Stylus
docs.text:
Note: This document was generated by Claude Code and has not been reviewed by a human. Please use it as a reference only.

The included stylus is a passive pressure-sensing pen. It does not require a power supply or Bluetooth pairing — pick it up and start drawing.

docs.title: Pen Button
docs.text: The stylus has a button on the pen body that works with supported drawing apps. It is currently compatible with ibis Paint X (more apps will be supported in the future).

docs.title: Set Up the Pen Button for ibis Paint X
docs.text:
Note: ibis Paint X must be version V11.1.1 or later.

  1. Open ibis Paint X, go to Settings → Supported Stylus, and select X3 Pro Pencil.
  2. Go to Settings → Stylus Settings → Button 1, then select the function you want (for example, brush/eraser).
